title: Ephemeral Connector Forensics Playbook (WIP)
summary: Working draft playbook for collecting, retaining, and reviewing forensic evidence for short-lived customer-managed connectors (ephemeral tunnels/proxies). Focuses on minimal-data footprints, approval gate integration, and rapid triage flows for customer private deployments.
body:
Context:
Short-lived connectors (SSH tunnels, transient VPN proxies, ephemeral sidecars) are a common pattern in customer-managed networking for Private deployments. They reduce setup friction but create gaps in audit traceability because endpoints and sessions exist for minutes to hours and then vanish. This playbook proposes a lightweight, privacy-aware evidence pipeline that integrates with approval gates and the operator handoff process.

Goals:
- Ensure a reconstructable timeline for any connector-related change or incident without requiring long-lived capture for all traffic.
- Keep evidence footprints minimal and PII-free by default.
- Tie ephemeral connector lifecycle events to approval records to support audits and post-mortem queries.
- Provide SREs and customer security teams a quick triage checklist and an evidence export format.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customer-managed networking means we cannot ingest raw packet captures by default.
- Evidence must be exportable to customer SIEMs (syslog/CEF) or stored in encrypted S3 with tenant-scoped keys when customers opt in.
- Retention defaults should be conservative (7–30 days) but configurable per contract.

Core concepts:
- Connector event envelope: one-line, HMAC-signed JSON string describing lifecycle events (create, auth, handshake, close, error). Includes connector_id (UUID), short-lived ephemeral_cert_fingerprint (sha256), origin_ip_cidrs (as masked prefixes), src_role, dest_role, start_ts, end_ts, approval_id if provisioned.
- Compact telemetry shard: periodic summaries (1min) of active connectors per host, aggregated counts, peak concurrent sessions. No payload/headers.
- Evidence bundle: when an incident is opened, the system can assemble a time-bounded bundle that contains event envelopes, telemetry shards, and optional enriched metadata pulled from approval gate records and KMS attestations. Bundles are signed and auditable.

Retention & storage policy proposals:
- Default: keep connector event envelopes for 14 days, telemetry shards for 7 days. Evidence bundles generated for incidents are kept for 365 days if the customer selects long-term retention add-on.
- Encrypted at rest with tenant-specific KMS keys for Private. For Dedicated, keys may be platform-managed unless customer requests BYOK.
- Indexed fields: connector_id, approval_id, customer_org_id, start_ts, end_ts, host_id. Index entries should not contain full IPs—mask to /24 or /64 depending on family, unless customer opts in for full-IP retention.

Approval gate integration:
- Approval records (approve/reject/auto-allow) must emit a compact approval-event that links to connector_id(s). Approval-event fields: approval_id, approver (human or policy id), decision_ts, decision_reason, requested_ops (e.g., open-ephemeral-ssh-to-host-xyz), ttl_expected.
- On auto-approval paths, generate a higher-fidelity audit stamp (policy_id and matched rule) so postmortems can show exactly why operators allowed access.
- For manual approvals, require an optional notes field that appears in the evidence bundle.

Triage checklist (quick):
1) Gather evidence bundle for the window ± 30min around reported time.
2) Verify approval_id matches connector event envelope(s).
3) Confirm ephemeral_cert_fingerprint was valid at start_ts; consult KMS signatures.
4) Check host telemetry for CPU/network spikes correlated with connector lifetime.
5) If payload-level analysis is required and allowed, request customer consent and follow data transfer checklist (legal + ops).

Forensic export format (compact-AUD):
- Line-delimited JSON with three sections: metadata (signed), events, telemetry. Each line is base64-encoded and HMAC-signed for integrity. Provide a small schema doc to SIEM integrators.

Operational playbacks & replay safety:
- Avoid storing packet payloads. When replays are needed for debugging, require explicit customer opt-in and provide ephemeral, time-limited replay tokens that can be scoped to a single host and expire immediately after use.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Risk: will /24 masking be acceptable for EU customers under gdpr when IPs are considered personal data? (Legal to weigh).
- How to represent multi-connector operations (e.g., a chain of ephemeral hops)? Do we create a parent-chain id?
- Decide default retention values through a cross-functional review with legal and SRE.
- Define UI/UX for approval-event linking inside the Console (quick filter to see "Connectors opened by approval X").

Implementation notes (proto):
- Agent-side: emit event envelopes to a local agent (syslog + sign) which forwards to the control-plane collector with tenant-auth token. Collector acknowledges with sequence id.
- Control-plane: produce an immutable event store (append-only) and a secondary index for fast lookup. Event store compacts older envelopes into daily rollups to reduce storage while keeping per-event hash for audit.
- Evidence assembly service: microservice that accepts incident_id + time range + optional filters -> returns signed compact-AUD bundle.

Sample event envelope (example, obfuscated):
{"connector_id":"c0a1b2d4-7f9b-4e2a-8a6b-e2f0fa123456","start_ts":"2026-02-14T09:12:03Z","end_ts":"2026-02-14T09:18:21Z","origin_mask":"10.20.0.0/24","host_id":"host-prod-12","approval_id":"APP-7889","ephemeral_cert_sha256":"b3f7...9c1a"}

Customer opt-in migration flow (minimal friction):
- Default OFF for deep retention (full ip, payload). Developer/Platform owner in customer console can toggle "enhanced forensics" per environment, with explicit checkbox to accept retention window and export rules.
- Provide a short migration checklist and small CLI helper to rotate keys and enable evidence exports.

References & related tickets:
- JIRA: PRV-901 (evidence pipeline spike), CONF:PLAT-4821 (privacy decision log), GH:PR-276 (agent signing prototype).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an early draft intended to seed discussion with Legal and SRE. Looking for feedback on acceptable default privacy tradeoffs, indices that are necessary for audits, and whether the compact-AUD export format is sufficient for common incident response tools.

Quick actions before next sync:
- @Liam to mock the compact-AUD schema and sample SIEM ingestion doc (Jira PRV-904).
- @Rhea to run short survey with 3 customers on IP-masking tolerances (deadline 2026-03-10).
- @Omar to prototype the agent envelope signer and publish sample envelopes to sandbox collector (PR in GH by 2026-03-05).

-- end of draft --
